description:
Every time you visit the dentist, one of the most common questions you are certain to hear is, “How often do you floss?” Every patient is different of course, and while some floss every day, others struggle to develop the habit of flossing.

The reality is that even if you brush twice a day, if you do not floss you are missing out on cleaning two-thirds of the surface of your teeth. Over time, plaque left in between the teeth and gums will harden into tartar and cause gingivitis.

Why eco-friendly dental floss is a good idea
Floss is specifically designed to get into the areas between teeth that a toothbrush cannot reach, and effectively removes plaque and bits of food caught between your teeth and gums.
While dental floss that is made of plastic may be good for your dental hygiene routine, it's not as good for the world around you. Plastic releases toxins into the ground when it's placed in landfill so choosing dental floss that is not made from plastic is a more eco-friendly option. Doing so means that you can maintain a good dental hygiene routine while also helping to take care of the environment that you live in.

There are 3 refills in each box and each refill is 33 yards long, so you can carry on keeping your teeth and gums clean for a long period of time.

Flossing does about 40% of the work required to remove sticky bacteria, or plaque, from your teeth. Most plaque hardens within 48 hours of formation, and within several days it will become so hard that it is almost impossible to remove. Tooth decay and serious gum problems can develop when plaque is allowed to build up on teeth and along the gum line.

The places where the gums and teeth meet are where flossing plays its major role. Tiny particles of food can get lodged here, and plaque in this area will harden and accumulate over time to form tartar, a thick deposit that only the dentist can remove with a scraper. Tartar buildup can lead to gingivitis: red, swollen gums that are the first stage of gum disease. If left unchecked, the bacteria-laden tartar and plaque can spread even deeper below the gum line, causing periodontitis: severe gum disease characterized by severe inflammation and eventual tooth and bone loss.

description: Dent-O-Care Extra Wide Flossing Tape 100m - The value pack of an extra wide Flossing Tape. A lightly waxed nylon floss comprising of extra wide filaments that splay on contact with the tooth, making cleaning under the gingiva easier and more effective. With the use of a toothbrush it is possible to clean only visible parts of the tooth and to a limited extent some of the area between the teeth. This however only constitutes about 70% of the total area of the tooth. In order to clean the remaining 30% it is necessary to use floss or interdental brushes to clean below the gum line. Like any discipline flossing takes practice, so don't give up at the first attempt. Dent-O-Care Extra Wide Flossing Tape 100m suitable for those who struggle or have limited dexterity we would recommend a holder which is particularly useful for flossing the back teeth. Instructions: Step 1: Take about 18 inches (50cm) of floss and loosely wrap most of it around each middle finger (wrapping more around one finger than the other) leaving 2 inches (5cm) of floss in between. Step 2: With your thumbs and index fingers holding the floss taut, gently slide it down between your teeth, while being careful not to snap it down on your gums. Step 3: Curve the floss around each tooth in a "C" shape and gently move it up and down the sides of each tooth, including under the gumline. Unroll a section of floss as you move from tooth to tooth. At first, flossing might feel awkward. But stick with it! With just a little patience and practice, it will begin to feel as natural as brushing your teeth.

Can We Brush Our Dental Calculus Away?
Your dentist will tell you that calculus is made of hardened plaque and the cause of nearly all gum diseases. A toothbrush is designed to clean only visible teeth surfaces but not dental calculus. Almost everyone has dental calculus. Scraping is the most effective way to solve it.

Our Story
We are a woman owned, small business. We set out with the Earth in mind – but also, individuals who want an aesthetically pleasing alternative to traditional plastic products. Our flagship product, Flora Floss, is designed to remedy the plastic waste that leaves our bathrooms on a daily basis – and we wanted to do it with sustainability and beauty in mind. Dent-O-Care Extra Wide Flossing Tape 100m suitable for those who struggle or have limited dexterity we would recommend a holder which is particularly useful for flossing the back teeth. Instructions: Step 1: Take about 18 inches (50cm) of floss and loosely wrap most of it around each middle finger (wrapping more around one finger than the other) leaving 2 inches (5cm) of floss in between. Step 2: With your thumbs and index fingers holding the floss taut, gently slide it down between your teeth, while being careful not to snap it down on your gums. Step 3: Curve the floss around each tooth in a "C" shape and gently move it up and down the sides of each tooth, including under the gumline. Unroll a section of floss as you move from tooth to tooth. At first, flossing might feel awkward. But stick with it! Why plant based floss?
Traditional dental floss is manufactured nearly entirely of petroleum-based nylon or plastic fibers ensuring that it takes well beyond our natural lifecycle to decompose. Regular flosses end up in our oceans, our local ecosystems, and ingested by or wrapped around wildlife. Standard floss is also composed of highly toxic chemicals calls PFAS's, a subset of perfluorochemicals (PFC’s), which according to the EPA, contribute to the greenhouse gas emissions currently aiding in global warming.
Kind floss features:
Our vegan floss comes with 1 33yd (30 m) spool of compostable dental floss and a refillable glass bottle fitted with an easy tear lip. Since our floss is vegan, you can rest assured that no animals were used or harmed in the making of the floss, making that pretty little cocoon that much better! Plant based floss is also slightly thicker than non-vegan floss, allowing it to reach those hard spaces and resist tearing.
Sustainability:
Our 100% Biodegradable and compostable floss products break down in approximately 6-12 months. The glass bottle your floss comes in is also reusable and all packaging is recyclable or biodegradable.
Ingredients:
Bamboo Charcoal Fiber, Vegan Candililla Wax, and Peppermint Essential Oil.
Our Story
We are a woman owned, small business. We set out with the Earth in mind – but also, individuals who want an aesthetically pleasing alternative to traditional plastic products. Our flagship product, Flora Floss, is designed to remedy the plastic waste that leaves our bathrooms on a daily basis – and we wanted to do it with sustainability and beauty in mind. You can look at that sweet little glass bottle each day and not only feel good about your impact – but also take it as a reminder to keep that smile healthy!

description:
Good oral hygiene involves cleaning our teeth daily, but we don’t always consider the effect synthetic ingredients found in conventional oral care, have on our health

Georganics was born as a result of Alex trying many high fluoride products in a bid to rid his unexplainable cavities, only to find they didn’t work. A change to his diet was the next option. A couple of months in, Alex decided it wasn’t just the food he was eating he needed to make a change to but also the products he was using; soaps, creams, deodorants…everything. He found natural alternatives for most things but struggled to find a pure toothpaste. Not one to give up, Alex made his own, left his job in the city and created Georganics.

Selling first at local farmer's market and seeing that some people were intrigued, some thought it was a crazy idea but others were relieved, they too had been searching for a pure and natural toothpaste for a long time. It was then that we realised that Georganics needed to reach more people./br>
Selling online was the next step. Customer feedback was positive, people were loving the eco toothpaste. These positive comments motivated us to experiment with the toothpaste ingredients and from this we developed the Toothpowder and Oil Pulling Mouthwash we know and love today. A few months later we took part in an accelerator course in Sussex. We fell in love with the rolling hills and green fields and decided it was where Georganics should be based. As demand grew and production picked up, Alex and Charles partnered up and as a result of we have now grown into one of Europe’s most trusted brands of genuinely natural oral health care.All three flavours of our new-look Georganics Natural Floss are certified PETA cruelty-free and suitable for Vegans. We make our natural floss from Corn Floss, coated with vegetable wax and organic oils. The floss is now also completely plastic-free so it can be composted.

description: Dent-O-Care Extra Wide Flossing Tape 100m - The value pack of an extra wide Flossing Tape. A lightly waxed nylon floss comprising of extra wide filaments that splay on contact with the tooth, making cleaning under the gingiva easier and more effective. With the use of a toothbrush it is possible to clean only visible parts of the tooth and to a limited extent some of the area between the teeth. This however only constitutes about 70% of the total area of the tooth. In order to clean the remaining 30% it is necessary to use floss or interdental brushes to clean below the gum line. Like any discipline flossing takes practice, so don't give up at the first attempt. Dent-O-Care Extra Wide Flossing Tape 100m suitable for those who struggle or have limited dexterity we would recommend a holder which is particularly useful for flossing the back teeth. Instructions: Step 1: Take about 18 inches (50cm) of floss and loosely wrap most of it around each middle finger (wrapping more around one finger than the other) leaving 2 inches (5cm) of floss in between. Step 2: With your thumbs and index fingers holding the floss taut, gently slide it down between your teeth, while being careful not to snap it down on your gums. Step 3: Curve the floss around each tooth in a "C" shape and gently move it up and down the sides of each tooth, including under the gumline. Unroll a section of floss as you move from tooth to tooth. At first, flossing might feel awkward. But stick with it! With just a little patience and practice, it will begin to feel as natural as brushing your teeth.
